recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless Vocabulary reintroduces a CodeSystem matching operation, in which case the output should preserve the historically applied 0..* unmatched cardinality.
issue_request: FHIR-12576 was a Published/Persuasive Vocabulary change request for the DSTU2 CodeSystem $compose operation. It reported that the out parameter compose.match.unmatched was 1..1 and should be optional because complete matches have no unmatched properties.
initial_application: The historical source was changed by commit 5df4188d5c9db25ee14a0c11e94ce44a1176197c on 2017-01-17, which changed compose.match.unmatched from 1..1 to 0..* in source/codesystem/codesystem-spreadsheet.xml. The 0..* result matches Grahame Grieve's contemporaneous Zulip guidance and explains the Jira resolution's endorsement of the change as made by Grahame.
additional_context: Later published issues FHIR-15956 and FHIR-17563 renamed CodeSystem $compose to $find-matches and cleaned stale references; both are already represented on the combined branch. Current source/fhir.ini includes CodeSystem as an active resource, but source/codesystem/list-CodeSystem-operations.xml lists only lookup, validate-code, and subsumes. Commit 40306e5cd9c1b1e3eb6f115de16a8da3aa13a351 later removed the CodeSystem $find-matches OperationDefinition from the current R6 source.
reconciliation: No source change was made. There is no current built CodeSystem $compose or $find-matches operation whose out parameter cardinality can be corrected, and editing orphaned examples would not affect the current specification.
